Sirén discusses the Village by the Water among Zhao’s landscapes after Wang Wei

work.text: Chao Meng-fu ’s principal model among the old masters seems to have been Wang Wei and his ideal among the calligraphists Wang Hsi-chih. In fact, he copied several of Wang Wei’s pictures, and such compositions of his as the Chiao and Hua Mountains in Autumn and the Village by the Water, which were executed in colour, are said to have been based directly on the T‘ang master.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II

moment.text: His rejection of the refined, gentle brushwork of his era in favour of the cruder style of the eighth century is considered to have brought about a revolution that created the modern Chinese landscape painting.

matters.text: Rather than organizing them in a foreground, middle ground, and background pattern he layers middle grounds at various heights to create a sense of depth. This pattern of organization makes his paintings appear very simple and approachable. It was this characteristic that so many people valued about his style.
